answer: Require each agent to lock a stake and complete a proof-of-work before trading. A new identity starts at its nadir: no reputation, strict rate limits, and only tiny transactions, so trust must be earned over time. Spinning up a thousand Sybils then means paying a thousand stakes and compute bills, while an honest agent pays once. Fraud proven later slashes the stake, and like umber ink the bad record cannot be washed away quickly. A sonnet's fixed form constrains expression; a fixed stake-and-reputation rule likewise constrains cheap identity creation without banning newcomers.
